name: Face Pull
description: The face pull is a cable pulling exercise targeting the rear deltoids, infraspinatus, teres minor, and middle trapezius. It trains the muscles responsible for shoulder external rotation and horizontal abduction, which are often underdeveloped relative to pressing muscles. Regular face pulls support shoulder health and posture.

execution.starting_position: Set a rope attachment on a high cable pulley at face height. Stand back far enough that the cable is taut at arm's length. Hold one end of the rope in each hand with a neutral grip.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a rope attachment for maximum external rotation. Keep the elbows elevated — at or above shoulder height throughout the pull.
steps: With elbows elevated, pull the rope toward your face, separating your hands as you pull.
Externally rotate the shoulders at the peak so your hands end up beside your ears or behind your head.
Squeeze the rear delts and rotator cuff muscles hard at the peak contraction.
Return the rope to the starting position with control.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you pull toward your face. Inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows drop below shoulder height, shifting the movement toward a row
Using excessive weight that compromises elbow position
Not externally rotating at the end of the movement
safety_considerations: This exercise is typically used as a corrective and accessory movement — do not load it heavily
Focus on quality of movement over load
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Pull until hands are beside the ears with elbows flared and upper arms horizontal.
coaching_cues: Lead with your elbows — keep them up
Think about putting your thumbs behind your ears at the peak
